Subdomains (regions) of a mesh

Source: R/mesh.R
mesh_regions.Rd

Every triangle of a mesh belongs to a named region (subdomain); by default all triangles belong to "domain". mesh_regions() returns the region of each triangle, set_region() assigns a region to the triangles whose centroids satisfy a predicate, and read_gmsh() takes regions from physical surfaces. Refinement keeps the region of the parent triangle. Regions carry piecewise coefficients through region_coefficient().

Usage

mesh_regions(mesh)

set_region(mesh, region, which)

Arguments

mesh

A pde_mesh().

region

Region name.

which

A function function(x, y) returning TRUE for the centroids of the triangles to assign.

Value

mesh_regions(): a character vector with one entry per triangle. set_region(): the updated mesh.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 4)
mesh <- set_region(mesh, "inclusion", function(x, y) (x - 0.5)^2 + (y - 0.5)^2 < 0.1)
table(mesh_regions(mesh))
#> 
#>    domain inclusion 
#>        24         8
